status: MEASUREMENT ONLY — nothing in this population was edited. Tier assignments are observations, not verdicts (I16/H7).

population.definition: tracked .ts files under platform/scripts whose module top level (column 0, no enclosing block) calls main()
exclusions_applied: pathspec limited to platform/scripts (no markdown, no 00_ARCHITECTURE prose, no 99_ARCHIVE)
every property detector ran over source with // and /* */ comments blanked out first, so a documented form cannot produce a hit

string and template-literal contents were NOT blanked, deliberately: SQL only ever appears inside strings, so blanking them would blind the (b) database detector. All 26 database-write hits were read individually and none is prose.
included_despite_path: platform/scripts/_archived/seed-abhisek.ts — under an _archived/ directory but a live tracked .ts file matching the population definition; flagged rather than silently dropped

criterion.source: D-67 part 2, taking it from M0-T60 finding rather than from file count
criterion.statement: THE HAZARD IS NOT "NO GUARD". IT IS WHAT HAPPENS ON INCIDENTAL IMPORT.
criterion.a: does importing it acquire a credential or open a connection
criterion.b: does importing it WRITE — database, filesystem or network

method_note: Because main() is called at module top level with no guard, importing the file EXECUTES the program. So the three properties are properties of the program, not only of its module-scope statements. A separate scan confirmed that NO module in any of the 76 import graphs performs a credential acquisition, connection open, filesystem write, network call or process.exit at ITS OWN module scope — every effect measured here is reached through the entry file main().

ratchet_allowlist.note: D-67 part 4 requires an itemised allowlist of exactly today population, GENERATED from this measurement and never hand-typed, with its count recorded so shrinkage is visible. PAY-DOWN ONLY: a file leaves the list when repaired; nothing is ever added.
